answer.summary: People assumed Apple would build the YouTube app better than YouTube could, and questioned why YouTube would give up default iPhone distribution. Mehrotra later called that way of thinking silly.

sections.heading: Mistaken assumption
sections.content: Mehrotra said people thought Apple would do a better job building YouTube’s app than YouTube itself could—“Who are we to tell them not to?” He called that assumption silly in retrospect. Apple also questioned YouTube’s decision because the app had default distribution on what Apple considered the most important operating system in the world.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately captures both mistaken assumptions: that Apple would build the app better than YouTube, and the attitude of “Who are we to tell them not to?” It is supported by the cited transcript and directly answers the question.
